chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding:
A man made his slave ride a beast of burden, and the beast trod upon a man. He (the Imam) said: 'The compensation is upon the master.'

key_terms.الْغُرْمُ: Compensation or indemnity paid for damage or injury
key_terms.دَابَّةٍ: Beast of burden (animal used for riding or carrying loads)

ai.seo_question: Who is liable for compensation if a slave's beast injures someone while riding under the master's direction?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on leases (*al-Ijarat*), this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the master bears the financial compensation (*ghurm*) when his slave, acting under the master's direction or possession, causes injury to a third party. This ruling underscores the principle of vicarious liability in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing it from cases where the slave acts independently, and highlights the master's responsibility for the assets and agents under his control.
